title: Recording: With A Little Luck by Wings | 1977
content:
Fair Carol, St John, US Virgin Islands
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineers: Geoff Emerick, Mark Vigars

Wings worked on the London Town song ‘With A Little Luck’ on 10 May 1977.

The session took place aboard the Fair Carol, a 105-foot yacht kitted out with studio equipment from the Record Plant in New York. It was initially moored in Francis Bay, St John, in the US Virgin Islands.

The backing track had been recorded by Paul and Linda McCartney the previous day. However, Denny Laine was suffering from severe sunburn, engineer Geoff Emerick had received an electric shock to his foot, MPL’s Alan Crowder slipped and broke his foot, Jimmy McCulloch had an ear infection which impaired his hearing, and Jack Crymes, ones of the support staff from the Record Plant, had a throat infection.

Because of these incidents, there was no planned session on this day. Instead, Joe English attempted to add a drum part to ‘With A Little Luck’, replacing the drum machine part that Paul McCartney had overdubbed the previous day. However, a final take proved elusive and the song was set aside for another day.
